cleanIntro: The KDS9c comes apart like a 1911 that has lost its bushing: slide stop out through the notch, slide forward, and then a recoil plug tipped out of the muzzle end. ⛔ Cup your fingers around the guide rod assembly as the slide comes off — that is the moment the spring is loose and unrestrained.

steps.title: Unloaded, inspected, slide locked back
steps.action: Muzzle safe, fingers off the trigger, unload it and LOOK into the magazine well and the chamber, then lock the slide back. Kimber's reason is blunt: otherwise the pistol may fire when you pull the trigger to release the hammer.
steps.quote: Make certain that the firearm is unloaded before beginning disassembly. Otherwise, the firearm may fire when you pull the trigger to release the hammer.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: Ease the slide until the tab meets the notch
steps.action: Pull the slide back to take the tension off the slide stop, then let it travel GENTLY forward until the semicircular tab at the rear of the slide stop lines up with the semicircular notch in the bottom left of the slide. Gently is the operative word — riding it under spring pressure past the notch is how the frame gets marked.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back, releasing tension on the slide stop and then gently let it travel until the semicircular tab at the rear of the slide stop aligns with the semicircular disassembly notch in the left side bottom of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: Slide stop out, pushed from the RIGHT
steps.action: Holding the slide in that position, push inward on the protruding end of the slide stop pin on the RIGHT side and remove the stop from the left. Both hands, both sides.
steps.quote: Holding the slide in that position, push inward on the protruding end of the slide stop pin (on the right side of the slide), push, and completely remove the slide stop from the left side.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: ⛔ Cup the guide rod as the slide comes off
steps.action: Guide the slide forward off the frame with your fingers CUPPED around the guide rod and recoil spring assembly. Kimber asks for that in the step itself, because on this pistol the assembly is free the moment the slide clears the frame.
steps.aside: Remove the slide by guiding it forward and off the frame.
steps.quote: Please make sure you capture the guide rod and recoil spring assembly with your fingers cupped around the assembly.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: Guide assembly out rearward, then TIP the plug out
steps.action: Lift the REAR of the spring guide first and withdraw the assembly toward the back of the slide. Then tip the slide upward and let the recoil plug come out. ⛔ Plug and spring are both under tension and Kimber wants eye protection on for this.
steps.aside: Remove the recoil spring guide assembly by first lifting the rear of the spring guide upward, then withdraw it toward the rear of the slide.
steps.quote: Tip the slide upward and remove the recoil plug.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: Barrel link forward, barrel out the front — strip complete
steps.action: Tip the barrel link FORWARD to clear the recoil spring tunnel in the slide, then slide the barrel out toward the front. That is the whole strip. ⛔ And with the slide off, do not pull the trigger — that would drop the hammer, which Kimber names in the same paragraph.
steps.aside: Do not pull the trigger, which would drop the hammer while the slide is removed from the firearm.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel by first tipping the barrel link forward to clear the recoil spring tunnel in the slide, and then slide the barrel out toward the front of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Reassembly

steps.title: ⛔ Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: The cleaning rod enters at the chamber, never the muzzle. Wet patch with bore solvent, let it soak a few minutes, dry patch to lift the loose debris — and read the solvent maker's own directions, because some of them will lift a finish as happily as they lift fouling.
steps.aside: Run a patch wet with bore cleaning solvent through the barrel bore and let the solution soak a few minutes.
steps.quote: Always insert a cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Wet brush through and OUT the muzzle, then repeat to clean
steps.action: Push the wet bore brush in at the chamber and all the way OUT of the muzzle before drawing it back — reversing a brush inside the bore folds the bristles over. Dry patch after, and repeat the pair until a patch comes out clean. Then a light oil, and ⛔ a dry patch through before you ever fire it.
steps.aside: Run a dry patch through the barrel before firing to remove oil.
steps.quote: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle, making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Breech face and every bearing surface — nylon brush
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off all the bearing surfaces on the slide and frame, then get into the breech face and the rest of the parts with a toothbrush or similar nylon brush. ⛔ And no ultrasonic tank: Kimber says damage from one is not covered by warranty, and night sights must never go near it.
steps.aside: Do not expose night sights to an ultrasonic cleaning environment.
steps.quote: Clean the breech face and all parts (a toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Lubricate by the drop, at the points Kimber names
steps.action: Premium oil, not grease — and if it carries Teflon, shake it, because the Teflon settles overnight and you will otherwise apply the carrier and none of the additive. Then oil only where this book says, in the quantities it gives.
steps.quote: Slide and frame rails; 3 drops on each side.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing in the firing pin channel, and wipe the excess
steps.action: Reassemble, work the slide five or six times, dry fire, then wipe off the excess. Moderation is the whole point: too little and it wears, too much and it collects the grit that wears it faster. ⛔ And if it has been stored oiled, a dry patch goes through the barrel before firing.
steps.quote: If the firearm has been stored with oil in the barrel and chamber, push a dry patch through the barrel before firing.
steps.cite: Kimber KDS9c Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

deepAbsentReason: Kimber's limit is printed in the strip itself — "The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning." — and again as a warning: "Do not disassemble your firearm beyond field stripping outlined in this manual. Do not manipulate any internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual." Going further voids the warranty in Kimber's own words. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Rod ALWAYS from the chamber end
Wet patch, soak a few minutes, dry patch
Wet brush in at the chamber and OUT the muzzle before drawing back
Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and parts with a nylon brush
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning — the damage is not warranted

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Premium oil, NOT grease; shake it if it contains Teflon
Only the points this model's book names, in the drops it gives
⛔ Never into the firing pin channel
Work the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe the excess off

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wiped clean; follower checked to slide freely

reassembly: Barrel into the slide from the front with the link tipped forward.
Recoil plug in, then the guide assembly in from the rear of the slide, rear of the guide dropped into place.
Slide onto the frame rails, run back until the slide stop tab lines up with the disassembly notch.
Slide stop in from the left and pushed fully home from the right.
Cycle the slide, dry fire, wipe off excess lubrication.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: work the slide five or six times and confirm it returns fully into battery, then dry fire and wipe off the excess oil. Check the slide stop is fully seated — a stop sitting proud will walk out under recoil. ⛔ A dry patch goes through the barrel before any live round if the pistol was stored oiled.
